issues.description: is_registered mutation on shared TritonLoraConfig is not thread-safe and breaks idempotency under concurrent requests
issues.detail: In _create_trtllm_generate_request, the code reads lora_config.is_registered, and if False, loads weights from disk and sets lora_config.is_registered = True. The TritonLoraConfig instance is shared across all concurrent requests for the same LoRA (it lives in TritonModelMetadata.lora_configs). There is no lock, no atomic compare-and-set, and no consideration of what happens if two concurrent first-time requests race: both will read is_registered=False, both will load weights, both will send weights to the backend, and the mutation has no happens-before relationship with the backend actually accepting the registration. Worse, if the backend request fails after is_registered has been flipped to True, subsequent requests will silently send only the task_id and the backend will reject them with no recovery path. State the precondition for is_registered=True: 'the backend has acknowledged the LoRA tensors for this task_id.' That precondition is never established by this code.

issues.description: Task-id assignment is non-deterministic across server restarts and across multiple model repositories
issues.detail: lora_task_id starts at 1 and is incremented in dictionary-iteration order over multi_lora.json across an outer loop over repo_paths. Python dict iteration order is insertion order, which means task_ids depend on the textual ordering of the JSON file and on the ordering of repo_paths. If a user edits multi_lora.json to add a new adapter at the top, every existing adapter silently gets a new task_id. If the backend caches by task_id across server restarts (as the comment implies it does within a process), the mapping from 'doll' to 'cached weights for doll' breaks silently. There is no specification of what task_id means as a contract between this code and the TRT-LLM backend. Refuse: state the invariant that ties (lora_name, weights) to (task_id) and enforce it, or derive task_id from a hash of the name/weights so it is stable.

issues.description: Defensive-as-substitute: bare `except Exception` swallowing all errors and returning None or printing a traceback
issues.detail: _parse_lora_configs has an outer `except Exception as e:` that prints the traceback and returns None. This conflates 'JSON malformed' with 'disk I/O error' with 'permission denied' with 'KeyError in our own code'. The caller cannot distinguish 'no LoRA configured' from 'we silently failed to load a LoRA that was configured.' In _get_model_metadata, lora_configs=None then means 'this model has no LoRA' and the model is happily served with no LoRA support, masking what may be a real configuration error. The new traceback prints in routers/chat.py, completions.py, embeddings.py are similar: print-and-rethrow as logging is sloppy; either log structurally or do not. This is defensive programming used in place of correctness reasoning. TESTED-NOT-PROVED at best.

issues.description: Variable shadowing: lora_config_path is rebound from the multi_lora.json path to model.lora_config.npy path inside the loop
issues.detail: Line ~671 sets lora_config_path = os.path.join(version_path, 'multi_lora.json'). Inside the TRT-LLM branch of the loop, lora_config_path is then reassigned to os.path.join(lora_path, 'model.lora_config.npy'). The outer-scope variable is now clobbered for any subsequent iteration of the outer repo_paths loop. A reader cannot follow the flow without simulating it. Rename one of them. This is exactly the kind of accidental name collision that structured programming exists to prevent.

issues.description: _get_lora_config can return None for a missing model_metadata, contradicting its declared return type
issues.detail: The signature is `_get_lora_config(...) -> TritonLoraConfig` (no Optional). The body uses `self.model_metadata.get(model_name)` which can return None, then accesses `model_metadata.lora_configs` without a guard. If model_name is somehow absent (refactoring hazard, race during model load/unload), this raises AttributeError, which then hits the bare `except Exception` print-and-rethrow in the router. The function also returns None on the lora_name is None / lora_configs is None path, contradicting the annotated return type. State the postcondition; make the signature honest (Optional[TritonLoraConfig]) and handle the missing-metadata case explicitly.

issues.description: Test for _parse_lora_configs no longer asserts the parsed result
issues.detail: The renamed test test_parse_lora_configs calls parse_lora_configs(...) twice and discards the return value. The previous test at least invoked the function; the new test exercises both backends but asserts nothing about the returned list of TritonLoraConfig. This is TESTED-NOT-PROVED: the test will pass even if the function returns wrong configs, wrong task_ids, or None when it should not. State the postcondition and assert it.

issues.description: Stray debug print(f'backend: {backend}') in the per-LoRA loop
issues.detail: Inside _parse_lora_configs, on every LoRA entry, the code prints 'backend: {backend}'. This is leftover debug output. In a server context, this floods stdout on every model reload for every adapter. Remove it; if logging is wanted, use the project logger with a single line per parse, not one per LoRA.

issues.description: Backend dispatch via `backend if self.backend is None else self.backend` silently overrides per-model backend
issues.detail: In _get_model_metadata, the call passes `backend if self.backend is None else self.backend`. When self.backend is set (e.g., 'tensorrtllm' globally), every model's actual backend is ignored and treated as TRT-LLM for LoRA-config purposes. The TRT-LLM branch then requires multi_lora.json to exist; for a non-LoRA model it does not, so the branch hits `continue` and silently yields no configs, which happens to be correct here but is correct by accident, not by reasoning. State the precondition: which backend's loader applies to which model? The current expression conflates 'CLI-declared global backend' with 'per-model backend' without justification.

issues.description: is_registered: Optional[bool] = False is a type-annotation lie
issues.detail: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered is annotated Optional[bool] with default False. It is never None in any code path; it is read as a plain bool (`if not lora_config.is_registered`). Optional advertises a tri-state that does not exist. Either drop Optional and use `bool = False`, or, better, eliminate the field entirely in favor of state that lives where the truth lives — the backend's view of registration. Annotations must mean what they say.

issues.description: Stale return-type annotation `None | List[tuple[str, str]]` on _parse_lora_configs
issues.detail: The function returns `None | List[TritonLoraConfig]`, not `None | List[tuple[str, str]]`. The annotation is stale from a previous iteration and lies to every reader and type checker. Fix.

issues.description: FIXME sed hacks in test.sh patch dims without a tracked issue
issues.detail: The test script uses `sed -i 's/dims: \[ -1, 3 \]/dims: \[ -1, 4 \]/'` on config.pbtxt files with a FIXME comment about a TRT-LLM version. There is no linked ticket and no termination condition for when this WAR can be removed. Either link an upstream issue or pin the TRT-LLM version this WAR targets so a future reader can verify the precondition still holds.

issues.description: Three identical print(traceback.format_exc()) blocks added across routers
issues.detail: chat.py, completions.py, embeddings.py each add `import traceback` and `print(traceback.format_exc())` before re-raising ServerError and Exception. This is copy-paste at three sites with no abstraction. If the goal is logging, route it through a single exception-logging helper. If the goal is debugging, remove before merge. Duplication is its own correctness hazard: someone will fix two of three sites later.

review.summary: REFUSED as currently written. The TRT-LLM LoRA registration protocol is implemented by mutating a shared TritonLoraConfig.is_registered flag with no thread-safety, no failure recovery, and no specified relationship to the backend's view of registration — DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE for a precondition the author has not stated. Task-id assignment depends on dict-iteration order over multi_lora.json and on repo_paths ordering, with no invariant tying (name, weights) to a stable task_id; this will break silently when users edit the JSON. Error handling is a bare `except Exception` that swallows everything and returns None, conflating 'no LoRA' with 'failed to load LoRA' at the call site. Tests exercise the new code paths but assert little about the parsed result (TESTED-NOT-PROVED); stale type annotations, a shadowed local (lora_config_path), and a debug `print(f'backend: {backend}')` left in the per-LoRA loop indicate the patch was not read carefully before submission. What would have to change: define the registration protocol as a contract with the backend and enforce it under concurrency; make task_id stable and specified; replace the catch-all with typed failures; assert postconditions in tests; fix the type lies and remove the debug prints.
